items.stem: How is multi-turn conversation state maintained across Responses API calls?

options.text: The application sends the needed prior context (or a state reference) with each request
options.rationale: Correct: the client is responsible for supplying context/state on each call.

options.text: The API automatically remembers all past calls for your key
options.rationale: State is not implicitly retained for you across independent calls.

options.text: State is stored in the client's CSS
options.rationale: CSS is unrelated to conversation state.

options.text: You cannot build multi-turn features at all
options.rationale: Multi-turn features are possible by managing context yourself.

items.explanation: Correct: the client is responsible for supplying context/state on each call.

items.stem: Which call is unsafe to blindly retry on any error?

options.text: A non-idempotent write that creates a record
options.rationale: Correct: retrying a non-idempotent write can create duplicates; it needs idempotency protection.

options.text: A read that returns the same data each time
options.rationale: Idempotent reads are safe to retry.
A stateless check is safe to retry.
A pure read is safe to retry.

items.explanation: Correct: retrying a non-idempotent write can create duplicates; it needs idempotency protection.

items.stem: Which TWO controls improve reliability of a production Responses API call? (Select TWO)

options.text: Retry with exponential backoff on transient errors
options.rationale: Correct: backoff handles transient failures without hammering the API.

options.text: Set a request timeout so a hung call fails fast
options.rationale: Correct: timeouts prevent indefinite waits and resource exhaustion.

options.text: Remove all logging to save space
options.rationale: Removing logging harms diagnosability and reliability.
Unconditional retry of writes risks duplicate side effects.

items.explanation: Correct: backoff handles transient failures without hammering the API.
